Across samples, the pause detector under-covers ground-truth silent regions (low recall) and includes false positives (low precision), while the initial opening/silence detector tends to over-extend or mis-bound the opening segment (e.g., overly long 0–~230s), which can swallow real content and misalign subsequent segments. A secondary contributor is segment post-processing: lack of standardized merging/deduplication/padding rules yields fragmented or overlapping removals that reduce IoU matching. Energy windowing granularity may also be too coarse for 2–5s pauses, hurting boundary alignment and sensitivity.","diagnosed_skills":[{"path":"pause-detector/SKILL.md","confidence":"high","diagnosis":"Pause detection guidance/defaults are too brittle for lecture-style audio with variable volume and short (2–5s) pauses, causing missed pauses (low recall) and borderline-speech false positives (low precision). Documentation lacks a practical tuning loop, parameter sweep ranges, and evaluator-oriented post-processing (merge/pad) to improve IoU alignment.","repair_instruction":"Add a task-specific “lecture video preset + tuning loop” section: recommend sweeping `--threshold-ratio` (e.g., 0.35–0.6), `--window-size` (20–60), and `--min-duration` (>=2s) using energy stats/plots; describe how to diagnose over/under-detection and adjust parameters. Include post-processing guidance to (a) merge pauses separated by small gaps (<=0.5–1.0s), (b) optionally pad each pause by ~0.2–0.5s on both sides to improve IoU while capping padding to avoid clipping speech, and (c) drop micro/low-confidence segments.
